label: Generating Functions
notes: This lecture, printed pages 20 through 26, asks how a single function on a base manifold can encode an entire Lagrangian submanifold of its cotangent bundle, and through the graph trick a symplectomorphism. We motivate the whole machine before unpacking the differential, the fiber-critical set, and the Hamilton-Jacobi link.

label: A Function Cuts Out a Lagrangian
notes: Start with the cleanest case. Any smooth function on the base has a differential, and the image of that differential is a section of the cotangent bundle. Because the differential of a function is closed, that section is automatically Lagrangian, so functions are the simplest source of Lagrangians.

label: Why the Section Is Lagrangian
notes: The tautological one-form pulls back along a section to the section itself viewed as a form. The graph of df is Lagrangian precisely when that form is closed, and df is closed because it is exact. This is the computation that makes a function a generator and explains the role of the canonical form.

label: Generating Functions With Parameters
notes: Not every Lagrangian is a section, so we enlarge the toolkit. Allow auxiliary parameters and consider a function on the base times a parameter space. The fiber-critical set, where the parameter derivative vanishes, projects to a Lagrangian that need not be a graph over the base, capturing folds and caustics.

label: The Fiber-Critical Set
notes: The construction lives or dies on a transversality condition. Demand that zero is a regular value of the fiber derivative so the critical set is a genuine submanifold of the right dimension. Then the horizontal differential supplies the covector, and the projection lands in a Lagrangian. This is the method of generating families.

label: The Graph Trick
notes: Recall how symplectomorphisms become Lagrangians. Equip the product of two cotangent bundles with the twisted form by flipping the sign on the second factor. A map is symplectic exactly when its graph is Lagrangian for the twisted form. So generating a Lagrangian here generates a symplectomorphism.

label: S(q,Q) Generates a Map
notes: Now write the generator in mechanics notation. A function of old and new positions defines momenta by partial differentiation, positive in the old slot and negative in the new. Solving these relations exchanges position pairs for momentum pairs and produces the canonical transformation. This is the classical generating function of the first kind.

label: The Solvability Gate
notes: The relations only define a map where they can be inverted. The mixed Hessian, the matrix of second derivatives in old and new positions, must be nondegenerate. The implicit function theorem then solves for the new position in terms of old position and momentum, exactly the gate seen in the notebook.

label: Hamilton-Jacobi and Free Motion
notes: Time-dependent generators tie directly to Hamilton-Jacobi theory, where the action solves a first-order partial differential equation and generates the flow. The quadratic generator minus half the squared displacement reproduces free translation, the worked example computed symbolically in the notebook with a unit mixed Hessian.

label: Geodesic Flow and Existence
notes: On a Riemannian manifold the metric identifies tangent with cotangent vectors, and minus half the squared distance generates geodesic flow, with constant-speed minimizers as the action minimizers. Finally, near the identity every symplectomorphism admits a generating function, since the identity sits just outside the degenerate locus.

label: Recap and Outlook
notes: We collected the through line: a function gives an exact Lagrangian, parameters and the fiber-critical set extend the reach, the twist turns Lagrangians into maps, and the mixed Hessian gates solvability. Generating functions are the bridge from variational mechanics to symplectic geometry, and they power the existence results ahead.
